subject: Acme AI — inference econ & next-step plan (Redwood vs hyperscaler)
messages:

Subject: Re: Intro / demo follow-up

Thanks for the walkthrough today — helpful context. A couple of things that matter for us as we evaluate economics: 1) per-1M token cost assumptions (incl. batching), 2) how cache hit rates change unit cost for our interactive assistant, and 3) whether Redwood can sustain 99th P95 latency at 512 tokens under our traffic profile.

Can you share a simple econ model and suggested tests? Also include any direct comparisons vs AWS Sagemaker endpoints and the managed OpenAI-like APIs we’re testing.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Torres
Director, Product
Acme AI

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme AI — inference econ & next-step plan (Redwood vs hyperscaler)

Sam — great to meet you and Priya on the call. Recap + immediate next steps below. I attached a lightweight econ model (redwood-econ-model.xlsx) and a one-page playbook for the test matrix.

Quick recap (TL;DR):
- Redwood unit economics: baseline numbers in the attached sheet assume gpt-like 8B model, FP16, with continuous batching at 64 reqs/batch and a 25% prefix cache hit rate. That yields our illustrative cost of ~$9.40 per 1M generated tokens (includes amortized infra + licensing + ops).
- Hyperscaler (SageMaker-like) comparison: same model/instance family but without Redwood runtime batching/cache optimizations results in ~1.6x higher cost for the same throughput profile; when you factor in additional dev/infra ops, total TCO can be ~2x at low cache hit rates.
- Latency: Redwood maintains 95th under 200ms for short responses (<128 tokens) on our dedicated pools; P95 at 512 tokens approaches your SLO — we should test with your exact prompt mix.

Proposed test matrix (short):
1) 1M-token run: simulate 1M tokens of production traffic with current prompt mix to capture perfornance + cost. (Outputs: tokens breakdown, p95/p99 latencies, infra utilization, cost.)
2) Batch sweep: run batch sizes {1,8,32,64} to observe per-token cost curve and latency impact.
3) Cache sensitivity: run cache hit rates {0%, 25%, 50%} — measure effective unit cost and tail-latency changes.
4) Hyperscaler baseline: reproduce the same 1M run on your current hyperscaler endpoint to capture delta.

Suggested owners / timeline: Redwood runs steps 1–3 in our sandbox (2 business days) and provides results + the model. Acme runs step 4 (or we can coordinate dedicated hyperscaler slot) in parallel. Then a sync to review (30m).

Next steps: I’ll schedule the sandbox runs and share the Drive folder. Ben, can you put together a short note on toggles (quantization, concurrency caps) we should vary? Marissa, please include any recent multi-model perf notes.

Attachments: redwood-econ-model.xlsx (summary tabs + assumptions), 1m-token-simulations.csv (scenario inputs)

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Acme AI — inference econ & next-step plan (Redwood vs hyperscaler)

Adding the quick engineering checklist and a few things to surface in the runs:
- Concurrency targets: emulate your peak conc (Sam, please confirm) — default test uses 120 concurrent sessions.
- Quantization toggle: test FP16 (baseline) vs 4-bit QAT/eager quantization to show cost delta. Note: Q4 runs increase latency variance at tails; we should capture p99.
- KV cache policy: run both full-context and prefix-only caching (prefix-only is more conservative but safer for correctness). Measure effective cache hit rate by request class.
- End-to-end trace: include token-level tracing for a 10k-user subset to diagnose any tail spikes.

I’ll own batching sweep automation; expect artifacts (CSV + charts) in the Drive by EOD for the sandbox run.

—
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Priya — thanks for the question. Quick answers inline: 

1) Per-1M token line-item breakdown: attached "redwood-econ-model.xlsx" tab "breakdown" isolates (a) infra-only (GPU hours + networking), (b) runtime ops (batching orchestration, KV cache infra), (c) platform features (rate limiting, tracing, console), and (d) account-level overhead. For your baseline scenario infra-only is ~ $4.75 per 1M tokens; add runtime ops $2.10 and platform/features $2.55 = total ~$9.40. We’ll produce the same breakdown for the hyperscaler run so finance can compare apples-to-apples.

2) Hyperscaler baseline: if you run the test on your account, we need: endpoint logs (request timestamps, latency percentiles), instance type and counts, and raw token counts per request. A short README in the Drive lists the required CSV schema.

3) Reserved pool estimate: yes — we can provide a non-binding 12-month reserved capacity estimate. I’ll have a draft MPA (attached: acme-mvp-mpa-draft.pdf) with a ballpark monthly commitment estimate based on the results of the sandbox run. That will include a simple escalation clause and a 30-day right to re-evaluate after the first quarter.

Next steps (action items):
- Redwood: run sandbox tests (Ben + Marissa) and drop CSV/artifacts to Drive by EOD Wednesday. (owner: Ben)
- Acme: run hyperscaler baseline or grant Redwood temporary read-only access to a test endpoint (owner: Priya).
- Redwood: deliver reserved-pool draft MPA after sandbox results (owner: Rachel).
- Schedule 30m sync to review results (I will propose times).

If that looks good I’ll send the calendar invites.

Best,
Rachel
